signal.headline: Range trade until $4,200 or $4,100 gives way
signal.reason: Gold rebounded after the hot CPI sell-off but is boxed between $4,100 support and $4,200 resistance, still under its 200-day average near $4,460. The Fed decision on 28 Oct is the next big catalyst.

long.why: A break above $4,200 opens the Oct 2 high at $4,230, then the R3 pivot near $4,300.

short.why: A break below $4,100 support points to the S2 pivot near $4,031 and the round $4,000.

posts.title: Gold weekly setup, week of 19 Oct 2026
points: Spot sits near $4,166–4,184 after a round trip. The hot September CPI print on 14 Oct pushed gold to about $4,090, then it recovered as the dollar and Treasury yields eased.
The Fed lifted rates to 4.00% in September, its first hike since 2023. Futures pricing points to a hold at the 27–28 Oct meeting, with one more hike possible in December.
The dollar was set for its first weekly fall in five weeks, which supports dollar-priced bullion.
Bull case: softer yields and dollar, Middle East risk and safe-haven demand lift price through $4,200 toward $4,230.
Bear case: another hot data print or hawkish Fed guidance sends price back through $4,100 toward $4,000.
Price remains well under its 200-day average near $4,460, so the larger trend is still corrective.
State Street keeps a base case of $4,750–5,500 by end of Q1 2027 but cut its confidence to 60%. The World Gold Council's base case was ±5% around $4,100 for the second half.
